verdict_reason: The organisation wrap around the entry guard is correct and needed, but it copies set-context.js's wrapping by hand, is untested (the NODE_ENV=test header fallback masks its removal), and leaves the add-a-set recipe describing the old guard.

todos.issue: The entry-guard onPreHandler (routes-live-animals.js:97-103) hand-writes the same request-context wrapping that contextualMethod in shared/set-context.js:100-105 owns: withOrganisationId(organisationIdOf(request), () => withSetContext(setId, ...)). Two homes for one rule about which context a set's lifecycle code runs in; the next context added (or a second set's gateway) has to remember both places.
todos.fix: Must: one function owns 'run this lifecycle method for this set with the request's organisation and set context', and both the route wrapping and the entry guard call it. One way: export a helper from shared/set-context.js (e.g. withRequestContext(setId, request, fn)) that contextualMethod uses, and register the guard as server.ext('onPreHandler', (request, h) => withRequestContext(SET_ID, request, async () => ...), { sandbox: 'plugin' }).

todos.issue: No test fails if the new withOrganisationId wrap around the entry guard (line 98) is removed. entryGuardTarget calls get(request, h), which reaches the backend through records/real/http/headers.js; under NODE_ENV=test headers() falls back to '5900001' when no organisation is in context, and no-set-singletons.test.js only counts withSetContext(SET_ID in onPreHandler registrations. In production the missing wrap would throw 'Cannot reach the notifications backend without an organisation' (500) on every guarded journey page, or send no owner scope.
todos.fix: Must: a test turns red when the entry guard runs without the signed-in user's organisation in context, proving the guard's backend read carries that user's Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id. One way: an injected request to a guarded journey path as organisation A against the real-records backend mock (nock) asserting the header value is A's id, not the test fallback; or extend the no-set-singletons source check to require withOrganisationId( in every onPreHandler registration.

todos.issue: The set-gateway pattern now also enters the organisation context around the entry guard (lines 97-103), but the recipe that describes it is unchanged: src/server/app/docs/add-a-set.md (rule 4 and 'The entry guard is an onPreHandler registered on the server ... the gateway re-enters the context around the guard itself') names only withSetContext. A new set built from the recipe would register a guard with no organisation and fail every guarded page against the real backend.
todos.fix: Must: add-a-set.md describes the entry guard exactly as the gateway now registers it, including the organisation context (or the single helper from the duplication finding that supplies both). One way: update rule 4 and the entry-guard bullet in add-a-set.md to name the helper the guard runs inside.
